title: Sessions: the timeline and the finder — the record of every visit searched, read on the Admin page and on the command line, by the owner only
request: The owner asked for everything that happens in DCLab to be stored in an organized, structured way that is clean and clear to find and understand; milestone A starts with finding and reading sessions.
spec: An Admin page Sessions (the latest visits: who, when, the problem and its family, outcome, spend, refusals, errors), a search by person, project, draft, kind of event, words, an error code and a date range, and a visit's timeline with links to its draft, project and jobs; GET /api/experience/sessions, /sessions/{visit}, /search; only the owner reads them. Done when 'every session where a build was refused' and 'every visit that touched project P' are one search each, on the page and on the command line.
plan: Give both logs (files and PostgreSQL) the same filters: person, kinds, a UTC window with the end excluded, many visits at once.
A finder over them: kinds, families and two groups (refused, errors) matching the session card; words only in what people and agents wrote; whole codes.
What a page shows: cell values never, model text only on request, people by name never by e-mail.
Three routes behind a new owner-only permission; the Admin tab with stat cards, a search bar, the list and a timeline.
The same search on the command line; review, plant faults, fix.

decisions.decision: A new permission 'timelines' held by the owner only, rather than reusing 'admin'.
decisions.why: The plan says owner and admin roles read timelines (proposed); 'admin' means changing settings and its refusal says so. A separate name lets the owner widen it later without widening settings.

decisions.decision: Words are searched in meta, person text and agent text; never in model text or a tool's values.
decisions.why: A search must not become a way to read what the page hides: prompts are kept only when the workspace keeps them, and a tool's arguments can hold a table's values.

decisions.decision: A code matches whole (case-insensitive), not as a part.
decisions.why: DCLAB-R1 must not find DCLAB-R17; a planted fault showed no test held this.

decisions.decision: The page's dates are the viewer's local days, sent as UTC times with the offset written out.
decisions.why: The page shows local times; a bare date was read as a UTC day, so evening events in the Americas and early-morning ones in Tehran fell on the wrong day.

decisions.decision: Refusals are filtered inside the read (SQL on PostgreSQL), not after it.
decisions.why: The 'refused' group reads every move and tool call; filtering afterwards let thousands of allowed moves fill the read's limit and hide older refusals.

decisions.decision: Error messages stay visible to the owner, as the contract classes them (agent text).
decisions.why: They are what explains a failed session; the contract notes a message may quote a value, and retention and redaction for export come with 19.10.

change: dclab_rnd/experience/__init__.py (read: until, user, kinds, visits, refused_only; _utc for every time given; refused(); cards() from one read), experience/finder.py (new), experience/__main__.py (search; show and search redact like the page; --model-text), agentic/pages/sessions.py (new: the three routes), agentic/pages/__init__.py and server.py (the log in the pages' context), accounts/guard.py and roles.py (timelines), web views admin.html (Sessions tab), home.html (a draft opened from another page), compute.html (a job opened from another page), Makefile (session-search), tests/test_experience_finder.py (new), CLAUDE.md, the capture plan and the roadmap.

findings.defect: The session card's family was an object, shown as {} on the page.
findings.scenario: The owner's 'Recording check' session in the browser: the API returned family: {}.
findings.cause: The problem card's family is a fact with a value and its source; the route passed the fact.

findings.defect: A code search matched any code containing the words.
findings.scenario: Planted fault: a substring match passed every test.
findings.cause: No test searched for a code that is part of another.
findings.fix: A test that DCLAB-R1 does not find DCLAB-R17.

findings.defect: The command-line search and show printed a tool's arguments (cell values) and prompts by default.
findings.scenario: A tool call with a customer's name in its arguments: `make session-search ARGS='--kind tool'` printed it; --kind model printed the prompt.
findings.cause: The text output printed raw events; only the JSON output went through the page's view.
findings.fix: Both commands redact to what the page shows; --model-text adds prompts for show.

findings.defect: The page's date range used UTC days while showing local times.
findings.scenario: An event at 23:59 on the 13th in UTC-5 was not found by From = To = the 13th; in Tehran events before 03:30 fell on the previous day.
findings.cause: A bare date was sent and read as UTC midnight.
findings.fix: The page sends local midnight as a UTC time with +00:00 (Python 3.10 cannot read a trailing Z; the server now accepts one too).

findings.defect: The page could not search by person or by draft.
findings.scenario: The plan's search names a person and a draft; only the API and command line had them.
findings.cause: The form was built from the audit tab's filters.
findings.fix: A person select (shown with accounts on, names only) and a draft field.
findings.test: test_a_person_and_a_local_day (the filter); the page checked in the browser

findings.scenario: The plan asks for links to the draft, the project and the jobs.
findings.cause: Home and Compute open a draft or a job only from their own lists.
findings.fix: A draft link opens it on Home and a job link selects it on Compute & jobs (a request through DC.state read by each page's enter).
findings.test: checked in the browser: the draft link resumes the draft on Home

findings.defect: A date out of range gave a server error.
findings.scenario: since=9999-12-31T23:00:00-05:00 raised OverflowError: 500, and a traceback on the command line.
findings.cause: Validation parsed the date but did not convert it to UTC.
findings.fix: One parser (_utc) raises ValueError for both; the route answers 422.

findings.defect: Refusals could be crowded out of a search by allowed moves.
findings.scenario: 30 allowed moves after a refusal with a read limit of 20: no refusal found.
findings.cause: The refused test ran after a limited read of every move and tool call.
findings.fix: refused_only inside the read: SQL on PostgreSQL, the same rule on files.

findings.defect: One read of the log per visit to build cards, and a long visit's card silently missed its first events.
findings.scenario: 50 visits: 50 reads, each globbing every file; a visit over 5,000 events lost its draft.created.
findings.cause: Cards were built visit by visit with the default limit.
findings.fix: cards() reads all visits at once; a timeline reads up to 20,000 events and says when it was cut.

findings.defect: No test went through the app as a non-owner.
findings.scenario: The mapping was tested but not the route's own refusal.
findings.fix: A reviewer principal patched into the guard: every route answers 403.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: each planted fault in the finder, the logs, the routes and the roles fails a test on its backend
measurements.result: 12 of 12 caught after adding the whole-code test (11 of 12 before)
limits: Only the faults planted; the page's script has no automated test here (browser-test not run).

measurements.name: page in the browser
measurements.gate: the owner's dev workspace reads as what happened: search, timeline, links, 375 px without sideways scroll, no console error
measurements.result: search by kind, words and today's local day found the recorded session; its timeline and the draft link work; no horizontal scroll at 375 px
limits: One recorded session in the dev workspace.

outcome: Every visit is found and read: one search answers 'which sessions were refused' or 'what touched this project', on the Admin page and with make session-search, showing what people and agents wrote and never a table's values.
lessons: A page that shows local times must send local days; a bare date is UTC on the server.
Two outputs of one command (text and JSON) must go through the same redaction, or the plainer one leaks.
Filter before a limit, not after: a limited read followed by a filter hides what is rare.
risks: Who else reads timelines is still the owner's decision.
A search reads the newest 20,000 events and says so; older ones need a date range.
